name: TinyPC - build a PC (open day)
description: Collect the parts, build the PC in order, shrink inside to see them fitted, then switch on, find the fault and fix it.

items.name: CPU (processor)
pages: The CPU (central processing unit) runs the program: it fetches each instruction from memory, decodes it, and carries it out. Billions of times a second.
This one has 8 cores (8 processors in one chip) running at 3.6 GHz: 3.6 billion clock ticks a second.
Underneath: over a thousand gold pads. Each one touches a spring pin in the socket on the motherboard.

items.name: RAM (2 sticks)
pages: RAM is the computer's working memory: the programs and data the CPU is using right now.
It is fast, but it forgets everything when the power goes off (volatile).
Two 16 GB sticks = 32 GB. Fitted in the right pair of slots, the CPU can use both at once (dual channel).

items.name: Thermal paste
pages: Thermal paste fills the tiny gaps between the CPU and its cooler, so heat can flow out of the chip.
A pea-sized dot in the middle is enough: the cooler squashes it flat.

items.name: CPU cooler
pages: A busy CPU can make over 100 watts of heat. The copper base soaks it up, heat pipes carry it into the fins, and the fan blows it away.
Without a cooler the CPU would overheat within seconds and switch itself off.

items.name: SSD (storage)
pages: The SSD (solid-state drive) keeps your files, programs and the operating system when the power is off (non-volatile).
It is slower than RAM but holds far more: this one is 1 TB. It plugs straight into the motherboard (M.2) and talks to the CPU over PCIe lanes.

items.name: Graphics card (GPU)
pages: The GPU (graphics processing unit) draws the picture on the screen.
It has thousands of small cores that work in parallel: great for graphics, video and AI. It plugs into the long PCIe x16 slot.

items.name: Power cables
pages: From the power supply (PSU): the 24-pin cable powers the motherboard, and the 8-pin cable feeds the CPU's power circuits.
The PSU turns mains electricity into the low voltages the parts need (12 V, 5 V, 3.3 V).

items.name: The monitor (PC off)
pages: Black: the PC is switched off, so nothing is being sent to the screen yet.

items.name: The monitor: black screen
pages: Still black. The fans are spinning, but the PC stopped at the memory check, before it got as far as the graphics: it has nothing to show.
A black screen plus beeps is a clue: count the beeps and look for a debug light.

items.name: The monitor: setup screen
pages: The setup screen (BIOS / UEFI): the PC passed its checks and found its parts.
It lists the CPU, the 32 GB of RAM and the 1 TB SSD. Next it would load the operating system from the SSD.

rooms.intro:
Your team's job: build this PC and get it to start.
The parts are on the two benches. Pick each one up to find out what it does (it goes in your bag), then fit them into the PC, one at a time.

markers.label: How much paste?
markers.text: How much thermal paste goes on the CPU?

options.text: A pea-sized dot in the middle
options.feedback: Yes: the cooler squashes it into a thin, even layer.

options.text: As much as possible: more paste, more cooling
options.feedback: No: paste is much worse at carrying heat than metal. Only enough to fill the gaps.

options.text: None: the cooler is metal, so it touches the CPU anyway
options.feedback: Two flat metal surfaces still leave tiny air gaps, and air carries heat badly.

options.text: The SSD has to be powered on first

Not this one: it's about getting your fingers to the slot.

rooms.name: The workbench: all fitted
rooms.intro: Everything is in. Press the power button.

rooms.name: The workbench: RAM fixed
rooms.intro: Stick pushed home, power back on at the wall. Press the power button again.

rooms.name: It works!
rooms.endText:
You built a working PC.
CPU: runs the program. RAM: working memory. SSD: storage. GPU: the picture. Cooler: takes the heat away. Power supply: power for everything.

markers.label: Summing up
markers.text: Which part forgets everything when the power goes off?

options.feedback: No: the SSD keeps your files with the power off.
Yes: RAM is fast working memory, but volatile.
The CPU has a little memory (cache) that forgets too, but the big one is RAM.

markers.label: Summing up
markers.text: Three long beeps at switch-on usually mean...

options.feedback: Yes. Like the stick that wasn't clicked in.
No: one short beep means all the checks passed.
Not usually: that's normally a graphics code.

markers.label: Summing up
markers.text: Why does the cooler need thermal paste?

options.feedback: No: screws hold it on.

options.text: To fill the tiny air gaps so heat flows into the cooler
options.feedback: Yes. Air is a poor conductor of heat.
No: it's about heat.

rooms.name: Standing on the CPU
rooms.intro: You're a few millimetres tall, standing on the CPU's metal lid. The chip itself is underneath, smaller than a fingernail.

markers.label: The lid
markers.title: The lid (heat spreader)
markers.text: The metal lid spreads the chip's heat out so the cooler can take it away. The markings say what it is: TPC-9, 8 cores, 3.6 GHz.

markers.label: Question
markers.text: 3.6 GHz means the CPU's clock ticks...

options.feedback: Bigger! Giga = billion.
Yes: 3,600,000,000 ticks every second.
Much, much faster than that.

markers.label: The RAM slots
markers.title: Next door: the memory slots
markers.text: Those four long slots are for the RAM. The CPU talks to the RAM through hundreds of copper traces in the board.

rooms.name: The RAM slots
rooms.intro: Four empty slots, clips open. You have two sticks.

markers.label: A1
markers.title: Slot DIMM_A1
markers.text: Memory channel A, slot 1. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: A2
markers.title: Slot DIMM_A2
markers.text: Memory channel A, slot 2. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: B1
markers.title: Slot DIMM_B1
markers.text: Memory channel B, slot 1. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: B2
markers.title: Slot DIMM_B2
markers.text: Memory channel B, slot 2. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: Which slots?
markers.text: The labels on the board say DIMM_A1, A2, B1, B2 (A and B are two channels). Where do two sticks go?

options.feedback: Both on channel A: the CPU could only use one channel. Try again.
Yes: one on each channel (dual channel), in the slots the board's manual recommends. Pushing them in now...
Both on channel B. Try again.

rooms.name: RAM fitted
rooms.intro: Both sticks are in slots A2 and B2. Each one should be pushed down until both of its clips snap shut.

markers.label: A1
markers.title: Slot DIMM_A1
markers.text: Memory channel A, slot 1. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: A2
markers.title: Slot DIMM_A2
markers.text: Memory channel A, slot 2. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: B1

markers.text: Memory channel B, slot 1. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: B2

markers.text: Memory channel B, slot 2. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: The clips
markers.title: Clips
markers.text: The clips at each end of a slot snap shut when a stick is pushed fully home. Have a good look...

rooms.name: The cooler
rooms.intro: Tiny again, behind the RAM. The tower in front of you is the CPU cooler, sitting on the CPU.

markers.label: The fan
markers.title: Fan and fins
markers.text: Copper heat pipes carry the heat from the CPU up into dozens of thin metal fins. The fan pushes air through the fins and the heat goes with it.

markers.label: Question
markers.text: Where does the CPU's heat end up?

options.text: In the air, blown out of the case by the fans
options.feedback: Yes: CPU to paste to cooler to fins to air, then out of the case.
The cooler only passes it on: it would get hotter and hotter otherwise.
No: it just warms the air.

rooms.name: The graphics card
rooms.intro: That wall in front of you is the graphics card. The SSD you fitted is hidden underneath it.

markers.label: Graphics card
markers.title: A computer in a computer
markers.text: The card has its own processor (the GPU), its own fast memory and its own fans, which face the other way. It gets data from the CPU through the PCIe slot and sends the picture to the monitor.

markers.label: Question
markers.text: A CPU has a few big cores; a GPU has thousands of small ones. Why does that suit drawing pictures?

options.text: Millions of pixels can be worked out at the same time
options.feedback: Yes: lots of simple jobs done in parallel. That's also why GPUs are used for AI.

options.text: Small cores are faster than big ones
options.feedback: No: each GPU core is slower. There are just far more of them.

options.text: The screen only needs one colour at a time
options.feedback: No: every pixel needs its own colour, many times a second.

rooms.name: Power in
rooms.intro: The 24-pin cable is plugged in: power for the whole motherboard.

markers.label: 24-pin power
markers.title: 24-pin power
markers.text: 24 wires: yellow = 12 V, red = 5 V, orange = 3.3 V, black = 0 V (ground). The green wire tells the power supply to switch on.

markers.label: Debug lights
markers.title: Debug lights
markers.text: Four little lights: CPU, DRAM, VGA, BOOT. At switch-on the board checks each part in turn. If it gets stuck, that light stays on.

rooms.name: Something's wrong
rooms.intro:
The fans spun up... then three long beeps, and nothing on the screen.
Find the light that's on.

markers.label: Debug lights
markers.title: The DRAM light is on
markers.text: The board got stuck checking the memory (DRAM = the RAM). Three long beeps say the same thing.

rooms.name: The RAM
rooms.intro: Look closely at both sticks and their clips.

markers.label: A1
markers.title: Slot DIMM_A1
markers.text: Memory channel A, slot 1. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: A2
markers.title: Slot DIMM_A2
markers.text: Memory channel A, slot 2. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: B1
markers.title: Slot DIMM_B1
markers.text: Memory channel B, slot 1. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: B2
markers.title: Slot DIMM_B2
markers.text: Memory channel B, slot 2. Two channels (A and B) with two slots each: one stick per channel lets the CPU use both at once.

markers.label: What's wrong?
markers.text: What's wrong here?

options.text: The stick in B2 isn't pushed all the way in: its clip is still open
options.feedback: Well spotted. Its gold contacts aren't touching the slot's contacts properly.

options.text: The sticks are in the wrong slots
options.feedback: No: A2 and B2 is right. Look at the clips.
No: it would still start. Look at the clips.

markers.label: Fix it
markers.text: Before you push the stick in, what do you do first?

options.text: Switch off and unplug at the wall
options.feedback: Yes: never fit or move parts with the power on.

options.text: Nothing: push it in while it's running
options.feedback: No! That can damage the RAM or the board. Switch off first.

rooms.name: Click!
rooms.intro:
Switched off, stick pushed down firmly: click, both clips shut.
Back to full size and try the power again.

rooms.name: It's alive!
rooms.intro:
One short beep: the start-up checks (the POST: power-on self-test) all passed.
Fans spinning, lights on, no debug light.

markers.label: Debug lights
markers.title: All clear
markers.text: No light on: CPU, memory, graphics and boot device all passed.
